intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Japanese hanami (flower viewing) tradition under hundreds of blooming cherry trees. Maruyama Park in Kyoto is home to a famous weeping cherry tree illuminated at night. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the season, and enjoy traditional street food stalls lining the park paths. A magical family-friendly cultural experience that defines spring in Japan.

experiences.name: Explore Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple in the historic Asakusa district. Walk through the Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon) and browse Nakamise-dori, a traditional shopping street lined with stalls selling Japanese snacks, souvenirs, and crafts. Kids and adults alike enjoy the festive atmosphere, rickshaw rides, and the chance to draw an omikuji (fortune slip). A perfect blend of history, culture, and family fun.

experiences.name: Day Trip to Hiroshima Peace Memorial and Miyajima Island
experiences.description: Take a deeply moving and educational journey to Hiroshima's Peace Memorial Park and Museum, then ferry over to Miyajima Island to see the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine. Families can reflect on history, spot friendly deer roaming freely on the island, and hike or take a ropeway up Mount Misen for panoramic views. A powerful combination of history, culture, and natural beauty.
experiences.location: Hiroshima City & Miyajima Island, Hiroshima Prefecture

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japan's legendary food culture at the Tsukiji Outer Market, still buzzing with vendors selling fresh seafood, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), matcha treats, and street snacks. Join a guided family-friendly food tour to sample sushi, grilled scallops, and Japanese pickles while learning about the market's history and Tokyo's culinary heritage. An unforgettable sensory experience for the whole family.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo district, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Togetsukyo Bridge Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most photographed natural landscapes, especially stunning during cherry blossom season when sakura trees frame the iconic Togetsukyo Bridge over the Oi River. Rent a rowboat on the river, visit the nearby Tenryu-ji Zen garden (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), and enjoy matcha ice cream from local vendors. A serene and visually stunning half-day adventure for families.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and purchase an IC card (Suica or Pasmo) at the airport for budget-friendly public transport throughout the trip. Take the airport limousine bus or train to your accommodation. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart — budget ¥500–800)
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and affordable meal at the airport or nearby convenience store upon arrival (onigiri, sandwiches, instant ramen — budget ¥600–1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy for the days ahead. Purchase your IC card immediately at the airport — it saves money on every train and bus ride. Convenience stores (konbini) in Japan are excellent for affordable, tasty meals available 24/7.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag with a slow morning. Enjoy a convenience store breakfast at the hotel. Explore the immediate neighborhood around Aegean Bliss Resort — take a leisurely walk along the beachfront, breathe in the sea air, and orient yourself with the local area. Visit a nearby local market or shopping street if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest major train station and take public transit to explore a nearby historic district or city center. Visit a local shrine or temple in the area — most are free to enter. Walk the surrounding streets and soak in everyday Japanese culture, street food stalls, and local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Find a local izakaya (Japanese pub) or ramen shop near the hotel for a budget-friendly dinner. Explore the beachfront at dusk for beautiful coastal views.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast — onigiri, tamagoyaki, and green tea (budget ¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Local ramen shop or soba restaurant near the sightseeing area (budget ¥700–1,000)
meals.dinner: Local izakaya near the resort — order house draft beer and small plates (budget ¥1,200–1,800 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day gently to adjust to the time zone. Japan is generally 13–14 hours ahead of US Eastern time, so jet lag can be significant. Stay hydrated and walk in natural light to reset your body clock.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early train to Tokyo (or the nearest major city hub). Head straight to Asakusa district to visit Senso-ji Temple — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Arrive early (before 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) and explore the temple grounds. Entry to the temple is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll along Nakamise Shopping Street, the traditional market lane leading to Senso-ji. Browse affordable souvenirs, try ningyo-yaki (small cakes), and pick up budget gifts. After Nakamise, walk along the Sumida River and enjoy views of the Tokyo Skytree. Cross into Ueno Park — a short walk or subway ride away — and explore the free park grounds and Ueno Tosho-gu Shrine.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ameyoko Market near Ueno Station for an exciting street food and shopping experience. Try takoyaki, yakitori skewers, and fresh fruit. This open-air market is vibrant, budget-friendly, and deeply cultural. Return to the hotel by train.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel breakfast (budget ¥400–700)
meals.lunch: Tempura tendon or katsu curry at a budget restaurant near Asakusa (budget ¥800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Street food at Ameyoko Market — takoyaki, grilled skewers, gyoza (budget ¥1,000–1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. Use your IC card on all trains. Nakamise Shopping Street opens around 10:00 AM. Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover 8–12 km today.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Kyoto via the Shinkansen (bullet train) — book tickets in advance for the best prices, or use a JR Pass if you have one. Arrive in Kyoto mid-morning. Head immediately to Arashiyama district. Walk through the iconic Arashiyama Bamboo Grove — one of Japan's most photographed natural landscapes. Entry is free and the experience is magical, especially in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the bamboo grove, walk to Togetsukyo Bridge for scenic views of the Oi River and surrounding forested mountains — particularly beautiful in April with cherry blossoms still lingering. Explore Tenryu-ji Temple garden (entry ¥500 — one of the most affordable UNESCO World Heritage gardens). Walk the quiet backstreets of Arashiyama and visit Jojakko-ji or Nison-in temples for minimal cost.
day_by_day.evening: Take a bus or train to central Kyoto. Walk along Pontocho Alley — a narrow lantern-lit lane famous for traditional restaurants and atmospheric charm. Window shop and enjoy the ambiance. Find a budget-friendly set meal (teishoku) at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store on the Shinkansen or at Kyoto Station (budget ¥500–700)
meals.lunch: Tofu cuisine or soba noodles near Arashiyama — look for lunch sets (budget ¥900–1,300)
meals.dinner: Teishoku set meal (rice, miso soup, grilled fish or tofu, pickles) at a local Kyoto restaurant near Pontocho (budget ¥1,000–1,500)

day_by_day.notes: The Bamboo Grove is free but gets crowded after 10 AM — try to arrive early. Togetsukyo Bridge is free. Consider a day bus pass in Kyoto (¥700) if planning multiple bus rides. April cherry blossoms in Arashiyama are stunning.

day_by_day.morning: Start early and head to Fushimi Inari Taisha — the iconic shrine famous for thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up a forested mountain. Entry is completely free and it's one of Japan's most awe-inspiring cultural experiences. Hike as far as you like — even 30–45 minutes up reveals stunning views and fewer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Nishiki Market — Kyoto's famous narrow indoor market nicknamed 'Kyoto's Kitchen.' Sample free tastings of pickled vegetables, fresh tofu, and Japanese sweets as you browse. Walk to Gion district, Kyoto's most famous geisha quarter. Stroll Hanamikoji Street and explore the wooden machiya townhouses. Visit Yasaka Shrine (free entry) at the end of Gion.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the cherry blossom illuminations at Maruyama Park, adjacent to Yasaka Shrine. This is one of Kyoto's most celebrated hanami spots, with a massive weeping cherry tree (shidare-zakura) lit up beautifully at night. Bring a picnic blanket and snacks from a convenience store for a classic hanami experience.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near your accommodation (budget ¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Street food tastings at Nishiki Market — skewered tofu, tamagoyaki, mochi (budget ¥600–1,000)
meals.dinner: Convenience store picnic for hanami at Maruyama Park — onigiri, edamame, canned drinks (budget ¥700–1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free and open 24 hours — early morning is magical with mist and minimal crowds. Maruyama Park cherry blossoms in mid-April are typically at or near peak bloom. The park is free to enter. A picnic-style hanami dinner is a quintessential Japanese cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) — one of Japan's most iconic landmarks, a Zen Buddhist temple covered in gold leaf reflecting in a tranquil pond (entry ¥500). Arrive early to enjoy it before tour groups arrive. Afterward, walk to Ryoan-ji Temple, famous for its mysterious rock garden — a UNESCO World Heritage Site (entry ¥600).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nijo Castle (entry ¥800) — a stunning feudal-era palace with 'nightingale floors' designed to squeak as an anti-ninja alarm system. The castle grounds also feature beautiful cherry blossom trees and traditional Japanese garden design. This is an excellent history and culture stop for families.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Kyoto city center. Visit a local supermarket (depachika basement food hall or a regular supermarket) around 6–7 PM when bento boxes and sushi are discounted by 20–50%. Pick up an affordable and delicious dinner. Stroll along the Kamo River in the evening — locals gather here to relax and it's a lovely, free experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (budget ¥400–700)
meals.lunch: Yudofu (hot tofu) set lunch near Kinkaku-ji or a budget ramen shop (budget ¥800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Discounted supermarket bento boxes or prepared foods (budget ¥600–1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Kinkaku-ji entry ¥500, Ryoan-ji ¥600, Nijo Castle ¥800 — total ¥1,900 for three major sites. Book Nijo Castle in advance online if possible. The 'squeaking floors' at Nijo Castle are a huge hit with children and adults alike.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Nara — just 45 minutes from Kyoto by Kintetsu Railway (budget ¥720 one way). Arrive at Nara Park, home to over 1,000 free-roaming sacred deer. Purchase deer crackers (shika senbei, ¥200) and feed them — a beloved family activity. Walk to Todai-ji Temple, housing the world's largest bronze Buddha statue (entry ¥800).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha Shrine (free outer grounds, ¥500 for inner treasure hall) — a UNESCO World Heritage shrine famous for its hundreds of bronze and stone lanterns. Walk through Nara's quiet, forested Kasugayama Primeval Forest paths. Browse the charming Naramachi district — a preserved merchant quarter with free-entry traditional townhouses.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by train. Have dinner at a local izakaya or gyudon (beef bowl) chain restaurant such as Yoshinoya or Sukiya for an ultra-budget meal. Rest and prepare for the next day's journey.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store before departing for Nara (budget ¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) — a Nara specialty available at local shops (budget ¥800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Gyudon beef bowl chain (Yoshinoya/Sukiya) in Kyoto (budget ¥500–700)

day_by_day.notes: Nara is a perfect family day trip — children absolutely love feeding the deer. The deer bow back when you bow to them! Keep bags and food out of sight as deer can be persistent. Round-trip train from Kyoto to Nara costs approximately ¥1,440 by Kintetsu.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Osaka by train from Kyoto (approximately 15 minutes by Shinkansen or 30 minutes by regular express — budget option ¥570 by Hankyu or JR). Head to Osaka Castle Park — the castle grounds and park are free to walk. The cherry blossoms in the castle park are legendary. Climb Osaka Castle (entry ¥600) for panoramic city views and excellent history exhibits about the Sengoku period.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Dotonbori — Osaka's most famous entertainment and food district. Marvel at the iconic Glico Running Man sign. This is Japan's street food capital: try takoyaki (octopus balls), okonomiyaki (savory pancakes), and kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers). Cross Dotonbori Bridge and explore the lively arcades and shops of Shinsaibashi.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Osaka's legendary 'kuidaore' (eat until you drop) culture. Visit a local standing sushi bar (kaiten-zushi or tachinomi) for affordable, fresh sushi. Walk through Namba area and enjoy the neon-lit streets. Return to Kyoto or stay overnight in Osaka at a budget hostel if preferred.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store in Kyoto before departing (budget ¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Street food in Dotonbori — takoyaki, taiyaki, and fresh crab claws (budget ¥1,000–1,500)
meals.dinner: Standing sushi bar or okonomiyaki restaurant in Namba (budget ¥1,000–1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Osaka is nicknamed 'Japan's Kitchen' and is a paradise for budget food lovers. Dotonbori street food is some of the best value in Japan. If traveling with children, the Dotonbori canal area is vibrant and exciting. Keep an eye on your belongings in busy areas.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Tokyo area or explore a final destination en route back to your hotel. Visit Ueno Park in Tokyo if not fully explored on Day 3 — the park is free and in late April may still have late-blooming cherry trees or beautiful green foliage. Explore the Tokyo National Museum (entry ¥1,000 — Japan's largest and most comprehensive history museum) for a deep dive into Japanese art and cultural history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's famous district for electronics, anime, manga, and pop culture. Even on a budget, window shopping and people-watching here is an extraordinary cultural experience. Visit multi-floor arcades (game centers) and try UFO catcher machines for ¥100–200 per play. Browse 100-yen shops for affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya Crossing — the world's busiest pedestrian scramble intersection — for a classic Tokyo bucket-list experience. Watch the crossing from Starbucks second floor (order a coffee for the seat) or the free Shibuya Sky ground-level viewing area. Walk through Shibuya's streets and enjoy the electric atmosphere. Find a budget ramen shop for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (budget ¥400–700)
meals.lunch: Udon or soba restaurant near Ueno (budget ¥700–1,000)
meals.dinner: Ramen shop in Shibuya or nearby — look for restaurants with plastic food displays and set menus (budget ¥800–1,200)

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo National Museum is excellent for history lovers and families — interactive displays make it engaging for children. Akihabara is a sensory overload in the best possible way. Shibuya Crossing is best experienced in the evening when it's busiest and most atmospheric.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed final morning. Return to any favorite spots or explore areas you missed. Consider visiting Yanaka — one of Tokyo's last remaining old-town neighborhoods, with traditional shitamachi atmosphere, free shrines, a historic cemetery, and charming craft shops. Walk Yanaka Ginza shopping street for affordable local snacks and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back toward the airport area. Stop at a large 100-yen shop (Daiso or Seria) for last-minute budget-friendly souvenirs — Japanese stationery, kitchenware, snacks, and beauty products make excellent gifts. Grab a bento from a convenience store or department store basement for a final Japanese meal before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart for the airport with plenty of time. Use your remaining IC card balance on transit. Return or keep the IC card — it retains value for future visits. Reflect on an incredible 10-day journey through Japan's history, culture, cherry blossoms, and family memories.

meals.breakfast: Final convenience store breakfast or hotel breakfast — try a Japanese-style morning set if available (budget ¥500–800)
meals.lunch: Department store basement (depachika) bento or sushi set — a delicious final Japanese meal (budget ¥800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or convenience store before the flight (budget ¥1,000–1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security. Narita Airport is far from central Tokyo (60–90 minutes by train); Haneda is closer (30–40 minutes). You can recharge your IC card balance in cash at any ticket machine. Japan's airports have excellent tax-free shopping for last-minute purchases.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Take the airport limousine bus or a pre-booked taxi for a comfortable late-night arrival. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) — try onigiri, sandwiches, or hot noodles. Budget ¥500–¥1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night simple. Download a translation app (Google Translate) and get a prepaid SIM or pocket Wi-Fi at the airport counter before leaving arrivals. Exchange some yen at the airport for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. After a leisurely breakfast at the resort, take a relaxed stroll along the beachfront area near the hotel to acclimate. Explore the local neighborhood, visit a nearby convenience store to stock up on snacks and drinks for the days ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest local shrine or temple within the area for a gentle cultural introduction. Many coastal Japanese towns have small but beautifully maintained Shinto shrines. Pick up a fortune slip (omikuji) and browse local souvenir shops. If near a town center, explore the covered shopping arcade (shotengai).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby izakaya (Japanese pub-style restaurant). Try local specialties such as grilled fish, miso soup, and seasonal vegetables. Toast to the start of your Japan adventure.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — enjoy Japanese staples like rice, miso soup, grilled fish, and tamagoyaki (rolled omelette). Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.lunch: Light meal at a local ramen shop or soba noodle restaurant near the hotel. Budget ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner with yakitori skewers, edamame, karaage chicken, and cold Asahi beer. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is your orientation day — no rush. Purchase an IC card (Suica or Pasmo) if you haven't already; it works on trains, subways, and even at convenience stores across Japan.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Tokyo via Shinkansen or express train. Upon arrival, head straight to Asakusa and begin your exploration of Senso-ji Temple — Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate), stroll the Nakamise Shopping Street lined with traditional crafts, snacks, and souvenirs. Arrive early (before 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Asakusa district — visit the Asakusa Shrine next to Senso-ji, then walk along the Sumida River promenade. Cross the Azuma Bridge for scenic views of the Tokyo Skytree. In the afternoon, take the subway to nearby Ueno Park, which should still have lingering cherry blossoms in mid-April. Enjoy a hanami picnic under the trees.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ueno's Ameyoko Market — a bustling open-air shopping street selling fresh food, clothing, and accessories. Have dinner in the area before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or grab a pastry and coffee at a local bakery before departing.
meals.lunch: Asakusa specialty — try a traditional tempura lunch set at a mid-range restaurant near Senso-ji. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Ueno Ameyoko Market street food dinner — grilled scallops, takoyaki, and fresh fruit. Or sit-down sushi at a conveyor belt (kaiten-zushi) restaurant. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. Nakamise Shopping Street is great for buying omiyage (souvenir gifts). Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover 8–10 km today. Check cherry blossom forecast for Ueno Park before heading there.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day early with the Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour. Arrive by 8:00 AM to experience the market at its most vibrant. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled seafood skewers, and matcha sweets. Chat with vendors and learn about Japan's legendary food culture. This is a fantastic family activity with something for every palate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning traditional Japanese landscape garden right next to Tsukiji. Enjoy the serene duck ponds, tea house, and seasonal flowers. In the afternoon, head to Odaiba, Tokyo's futuristic waterfront island. Families can enjoy teamLab Borderless digital art museum (book in advance) or explore DiverCity Tokyo Plaza.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over Tokyo Bay from Odaiba's waterfront promenade, with views of the Rainbow Bridge and the city skyline. Dine at Odaiba's Aqua City or Palette Town mall, which offer diverse mid-range dining options.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh sushi breakfast, tamagoyaki, and green tea. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 for sampling.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Hamarikyu Gardens tea house — matcha and wagashi (traditional sweets). Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Odaiba mall restaurant — try a family-friendly shabu-shabu (hot pot) or teppanyaki restaurant. Budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is free to walk through — just buy what you taste. Book teamLab Borderless well in advance as it sells out quickly. Hamarikyu Gardens entry fee is ¥300 per adult. Odaiba is very family-friendly with wide open spaces.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen (bullet train) from Tokyo to Kyoto — a highlight experience in itself (approx. 2h 15min on the Nozomi). Arrive in Kyoto and check your day bag into a coin locker at Kyoto Station. Head directly to Arashiyama — take the JR Sagano Line. Begin the morning at the iconic Arashiyama Bamboo Grove, wandering the ethereal towering bamboo tunnels. Arrive before 9:00 AM for the most magical, crowd-free experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the scenic Togetsukyo Bridge over the Oi River with views of the forested Arashiyama mountains. Visit Tenryu-ji Temple and its UNESCO-listed garden. Stroll the charming Sagano Romantic Train area and the preserved townscape of Saga-Toriimoto. If cherry blossoms are still blooming, Arashiyama is spectacular in mid-April.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto. Explore the Gion district as dusk falls — the historic geisha quarter with traditional wooden machiya townhouses. You may spot a maiko (apprentice geisha) on her way to an evening appointment. Dine in Gion or Pontocho Alley.

meals.breakfast: Grab an ekiben (station bento box) at Tokyo Station before boarding the Shinkansen. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.lunch: Arashiyama tofu cuisine — Kyoto is famous for yudofu (hot tofu). Try a tofu kaiseki set lunch near Tenryu-ji. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,000.
meals.dinner: Pontocho Alley dinner — narrow lantern-lit alley packed with atmospheric restaurants. Try Kyoto-style kaiseki or yakitori. Budget ¥3,000–¥5,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a JR Pass if you haven't already — it covers the Shinkansen and many regional trains. Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is free to walk through. Tenryu-ji garden entry is ¥500. Gion is best explored on foot in the early evening.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Kyoto focused on history and culture. Start early at Fushimi Inari Taisha — the famous shrine with thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up a forested mountain. Hike as far as you're comfortable (even 30 minutes up gives spectacular views). This is one of Japan's most iconic and photogenic sites, free to visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Higashiyama district — Kyoto's best-preserved historic neighborhood. Walk the stone-paved Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka lanes lined with traditional shops and teahouses. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple perched dramatically on a hillside with sweeping city views. Explore Kodai-ji Temple and its beautiful moss gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Nishiki Market — Kyoto's 'Kitchen' — a narrow covered market with over 100 stalls selling pickles, fresh tofu, grilled skewers, and local delicacies. Perfect for snacking and souvenir shopping. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in the Kawaramachi entertainment district.

meals.breakfast: Early morning at a local Kyoto kissaten (coffee shop) or convenience store near your day base. Budget ¥500–¥1,000.
meals.lunch: Higashiyama area — try a matcha soba set or a traditional obanzai (Kyoto home-style cuisine) lunch. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Kawaramachi restaurant — try Kyoto-style ramen or a mid-range izakaya with local sake. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500.

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free and open 24/7 — arrive before 8:00 AM to avoid crowds. Kiyomizudera entry is ¥500. Wear comfortable shoes for the hillside walking in Higashiyama. Nishiki Market is free to browse — budget ¥1,000–¥2,000 for tastings.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — Kyoto's most famous hanami spot, centered around the iconic weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura). In mid-April, late-blooming varieties may still be flowering. Spread out a picnic blanket and enjoy the quintessential Japanese hanami experience. The park is free and very family-friendly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the adjacent Yasaka Shrine and the Chion-in Temple — one of Japan's largest and most impressive Buddhist temple complexes. Walk through the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku no Michi), a 2 km stone-paved canal-side walkway lined with cherry trees, connecting Nanzen-ji to Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion). Visit Nanzen-ji Temple and its dramatic aqueduct.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort via Shinkansen or overnight bus. Alternatively, spend the night in Kyoto if budget allows for one night at a mid-range ryokan (traditional inn) for an authentic cultural experience. Enjoy a quiet evening dinner.

meals.breakfast: Maruyama Park hanami picnic breakfast — pick up onigiri, sandwiches, and drinks from a nearby convenience store or Nishiki Market. Budget ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.lunch: Nanzen-ji area — try a yudofu (hot tofu) restaurant, a Kyoto specialty. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,000.
meals.dinner: Farewell Kyoto dinner — try a mid-range tempura or sukiyaki restaurant in the city center. Budget ¥3,000–¥4,500.

day_by_day.notes: Maruyama Park is free. Philosopher's Path is free. Nanzen-ji entry is ¥500. If opting for a ryokan night, budget ¥12,000–¥20,000 per room including dinner and breakfast — a worthwhile splurge for the cultural experience. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Hiroshima — take the Shinkansen from Kyoto (or Shin-Osaka) to Hiroshima (approx. 1.5 hours). Begin with the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park and Museum. This deeply moving and historically significant site is essential for families and history lovers. The A-Bomb Dome, Children's Peace Monument, and the museum provide a profound and educational experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Peace Memorial, take the ferry from Ujina Port (or Miyajimaguchi) to Miyajima Island (Itsukushima). Witness the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine at high or low tide — both offer different but equally stunning views. Explore the island's deer (they roam freely!), Daisho-in Temple, and the five-story pagoda. Try local Miyajima oysters and momiji manju (maple leaf cakes).
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry and Shinkansen back toward your base. Have dinner in Hiroshima city before departing — try Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki, a layered savory pancake that is completely different from Osaka style and a must-try local specialty.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or grab food at the Shinkansen station. Budget ¥800–¥1,500.
meals.lunch: Miyajima Island — fresh grilled oysters, oyster rice, and momiji manju from island vendors. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Hiroshima Okonomimura (a multi-floor building dedicated to okonomiyaki) — try the Hiroshima-style layered pancake with noodles and egg. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,800.

day_by_day.notes: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum entry is ¥200 per adult. Miyajima ferry is approximately ¥180 each way (covered by JR Pass). Itsukushima Shrine entry is ¥300. The floating torii is best photographed at high tide — check tide tables in advance. This is a long day, so start early (depart by 7:30 AM).

day_by_day.morning: Return to the resort area for a relaxed morning. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast and take time to explore the beachfront surroundings. Visit any local historical sites, shrines, or cultural spots near the resort that you haven't yet explored. This is a good day to rest your feet after the intense travel days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon beach walk or water activity near the resort. Explore the local town — browse craft shops, try local sweets at a wagashi (traditional confectionery) shop, and visit a local onsen (hot spring bath) if available nearby. A traditional onsen soak is a perfect way to relax tired muscles and experience authentic Japanese bathing culture.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell family dinner at the resort or a special local restaurant. Celebrate the trip with a kaiseki-inspired set meal or a fresh seafood dinner, reflecting on the incredible experiences of the past 10 days. Let the kids pick their favorite Japanese dish of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — enjoy it slowly. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near the resort — try a fresh seafood donburi (rice bowl) with local catch. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at the resort or a nearby mid-range restaurant — fresh sashimi, grilled fish, miso soup, and seasonal vegetables. Budget ¥3,000–¥5,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Onsen etiquette: tattoos may be restricted at some facilities. Bring a small towel. Children are generally welcome at family onsen (kazoku-buro private baths). This is a great day to do last-minute souvenir shopping and pack gifts for home.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a final sunrise walk along the beach or resort gardens. Enjoy a last Japanese breakfast — savor the miso soup, pickled vegetables, and steamed rice one final time. Begin packing and prepare for checkout. Store luggage with the concierge if your flight is in the afternoon or evening.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, take a final short excursion to a nearby attraction — a local shrine, garden, or viewpoint. Do any last-minute shopping for omiyage (gifts) at a local department store or airport. Head to the airport with plenty of time — aim to arrive 3 hours before international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Check in at the airport, clear security, and browse the duty-free shops. Japan's airports have excellent shopping and dining — pick up Japanese Kit-Kats, sake, cosmetics, and snacks as final gifts. Board your flight home filled with wonderful memories.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — make it count! Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the resort or at the airport. Try one last bowl of ramen or a tonkatsu set. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Airport terminal restaurant or in-flight meal. Treat yourself to one last sushi set at the airport. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for airport check-in with families and luggage. Japan's airports (Narita, Haneda, Kansai) are very well organized. Reclaim your tax refund (消費税免税) at the airport customs counter if you made qualifying purchases. Don't forget to return your pocket Wi-Fi device at the airport counter.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Japanese hanami (flower viewing) tradition under hundreds of blooming cherry trees. Maruyama Park in Kyoto is home to a famous weeping cherry tree illuminated at night. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the season, and enjoy traditional street food stalls lining the park paths. A magical family-friendly cultural experience that defines spring in Japan.

experiences.name: Explore Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple in the historic Asakusa district. Walk through the Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon) and browse Nakamise-dori, a traditional shopping street lined with stalls selling Japanese snacks, souvenirs, and crafts. Kids and adults alike enjoy the festive atmosphere, rickshaw rides, and the chance to draw an omikuji (fortune slip). A perfect blend of history, culture, and family fun.

experiences.name: Day Trip to Hiroshima Peace Memorial and Miyajima Island
experiences.description: Take a deeply moving and educational journey to Hiroshima's Peace Memorial Park and Museum, then ferry over to Miyajima Island to see the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine. Families can reflect on history, spot friendly deer roaming freely on the island, and hike or take a ropeway up Mount Misen for panoramic views. A powerful combination of history, culture, and natural beauty.
experiences.location: Hiroshima City & Miyajima Island, Hiroshima Prefecture

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japan's legendary food culture at the Tsukiji Outer Market, still buzzing with vendors selling fresh seafood, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), matcha treats, and street snacks. Join a guided family-friendly food tour to sample sushi, grilled scallops, and Japanese pickles while learning about the market's history and Tokyo's culinary heritage. An unforgettable sensory experience for the whole family.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo district, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Togetsukyo Bridge Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most photographed natural landscapes, especially stunning during cherry blossom season when sakura trees frame the iconic Togetsukyo Bridge over the Oi River. Rent a rowboat on the river, visit the nearby Tenryu-ji Zen garden (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), and enjoy matcha ice cream from local vendors. A serene and visually stunning half-day adventure for families.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to escort you to the Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a late-night welcome amenity prepared by the hotel — chilled sake, seasonal wagashi sweets, and a warm oshibori towel. Check in, unwind, and prepare for the journey ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light in-room dining from the hotel's curated late-night menu — try the seasonal kaiseki bento box and miso soup, available until midnight.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day only. No sightseeing scheduled. Confirm private transfer booking in advance. Request early check-in amenities if the hotel offers them for late arrivals. Keep luggage minimal for easy transfer.

day_by_day.morning: Begin your first full day with a leisurely breakfast at the resort, then take a private guided tour of the nearby Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street in the historic Asakusa district. Arrive early (around 8:00 AM) to beat the crowds and experience the temple in a serene, golden morning light. Your guide will share the temple's 1,400-year history and help you participate in the traditional omikuji fortune-drawing ritual.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Nakamise Shopping Street to browse premium Japanese crafts, handmade fans, lacquerware, and seasonal cherry blossom souvenirs. Transition to the upscale Omotesando district for a curated cultural walk through its blend of contemporary architecture and traditional Japanese aesthetics. Visit the Nezu Museum, home to a stunning collection of pre-modern Asian art and a tranquil Japanese garden.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant in the Ginza district for a multi-course dinner celebrating the spring season. Afterward, take a relaxing evening stroll along the illuminated Sumida River, where cherry blossom trees line the banks in full bloom.

meals.breakfast: In-resort breakfast featuring a Japanese-Western fusion spread — fresh sashimi, tamago gohan, croissants, and seasonal fruit.
meals.lunch: Tempura Kondo (Ginza) — renowned for its exquisite seasonal vegetable and seafood tempura in an intimate, refined setting.
meals.dinner: Kikunoi Akasaka — a celebrated Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant offering an 8-course spring tasting menu with sake pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. The Nezu Museum charges a modest admission fee. Book Kikunoi well in advance as reservations are highly competitive. Dress smart-casual for dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on an immersive Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour with a private guide. Arrive by 8:00 AM to witness the bustling morning energy of Japan's most iconic food market. Sample fresh uni (sea urchin), tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), premium tuna sashimi, matcha confections, and artisan pickles. Learn about Japan's deep culinary heritage and the art of fish selection directly from seasoned vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to the Imperial Palace East Gardens for a peaceful afternoon walk through meticulously maintained traditional Japanese gardens, still graced by late-blooming cherry blossoms in mid-April. Follow with a visit to the Edo-Tokyo Museum (or its annex if undergoing renovation) for a fascinating deep-dive into Tokyo's transformation from a feudal city to a modern metropolis — perfect for history enthusiasts.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a private tea ceremony experience at a historic machiya townhouse in the Yanaka district, one of Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhoods. Conclude the evening with dinner at a high-end teppanyaki restaurant where a master chef prepares A5 Wagyu beef tableside.

meals.breakfast: Street breakfast during the Tsukiji tour — fresh tuna sashimi, tamagoyaki, and matcha soft-serve from market stalls.
meals.lunch: Sushi Saito (if reservations secured) or Harutaka in Ginza — intimate omakase sushi with the finest seasonal ingredients.
meals.dinner: Ukai-tei Omotesando — a prestigious teppanyaki restaurant serving A5 Wagyu beef and seasonal vegetables in an elegant atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji tours should be pre-booked with a reputable luxury guide company. The private tea ceremony requires advance reservation — coordinate through the hotel concierge. Omakase sushi restaurants often require reservations weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for Kyoto via the Shinkansen (bullet train) — a quintessential Japanese experience in itself. Book Green Car (first class) seats for a premium ride with views of Mount Fuji on clear days. Upon arrival in Kyoto, check in to your pre-arranged luxury suite at a renowned ryokan (traditional inn). Begin the afternoon with a visit to the Arashiyama Bamboo Grove, wandering through the towering green corridors in the soft morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Arashiyama with a walk across the iconic Togetsukyo Bridge, framed by cherry blossoms and mountain scenery. Visit Tenryu-ji Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with a breathtaking Zen garden and koi-filled pond. Take a private rickshaw (jinrikisha) ride through the quiet lanes of Sagano, passing traditional farmhouses and bamboo-lined paths.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the ryokan for a private onsen (hot spring bath) experience followed by a full multi-course kaiseki dinner served in your room by kimono-clad attendants — a deeply immersive and luxurious Japanese cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the Tokyo hotel or an ekiben (premium station bento) enjoyed on the Shinkansen.
meals.lunch: Shoraian — a picturesque riverside restaurant in Arashiyama serving refined tofu kaiseki cuisine with views of the Oi River.
meals.dinner: In-room kaiseki dinner at the ryokan — a seasonal 10-course meal featuring Kyoto-style delicacies such as yudofu, kyo-yasai vegetables, and wagyu.

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen Green Car tickets well in advance, especially during cherry blossom season (peak tourism). Rickshaw rides in Arashiyama should be pre-arranged. Confirm ryokan check-in time and request early arrival if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a serene cherry blossom viewing experience at Maruyama Park in Kyoto — the city's most beloved hanami destination. The park's famous weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) is a spectacular sight, especially in the soft morning light before crowds arrive. Enjoy a private picnic breakfast prepared by the ryokan under the blossoms — a truly once-in-a-lifetime hanami experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Higashiyama district on foot — a beautifully preserved stretch of traditional machiya townhouses, stone-paved lanes, and ancient shrines. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple, perched dramatically on a hillside with sweeping views over Kyoto's cherry blossom canopy. Continue to Yasaka Shrine and Kodai-ji Temple, where moss gardens and lantern-lit pathways create an atmosphere of timeless elegance.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a private Maiko (apprentice geisha) dinner performance in Gion, Kyoto's famous geisha district. Enjoy traditional Kyoto cuisine while being entertained by classical dance, shamisen music, and ozashiki games — a rare and exclusive cultural encounter arranged through the hotel concierge.

meals.breakfast: Private ryokan-prepared hanami picnic basket — onigiri, dashimaki tamago, seasonal pickles, matcha, and wagashi under the cherry blossoms.
meals.lunch: Mizai — a Michelin three-star kaiseki restaurant in Higashiyama offering an exceptional seasonal lunch course.
meals.dinner: Private ozashiki dinner in Gion with a Maiko performance — traditional Kyoto cuisine including obanzai dishes, seasonal sashimi, and premium sake.

day_by_day.notes: Maiko dinner experiences are extremely exclusive and must be booked weeks in advance through a specialized cultural experience agency or the hotel concierge. Kiyomizudera may be crowded — arrive before 9:00 AM for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private guided morning tour of Nijo Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and former residence of the Tokugawa shoguns. Admire the ornate Ninomaru Palace interiors, the famous 'nightingale floors' that chirp underfoot as a security measure, and the castle's stunning cherry blossom gardens still in bloom in mid-April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Kyoto Imperial Palace and its surrounding Kyoto Gyoen National Garden — a vast, tranquil park dotted with cherry trees and traditional architecture. Join a guided tour of the palace grounds (advance reservation required). Afterward, explore the Nishiki Market — Kyoto's 'Kitchen' — for premium tastings of local street foods, artisan tofu, and specialty Japanese ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset visit to Fushimi Inari Shrine, hiking through the iconic vermilion torii gate tunnels as the light fades and the crowds thin. Return to the ryokan for a relaxing evening onsen soak and a light in-room supper.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at the ryokan — grilled fish, miso soup, rice, pickles, tofu, and tamago.
meals.lunch: Nishiki Market tasting lunch — premium street foods including fresh yuba (tofu skin), Kyoto pickles, wagyu skewers, and matcha parfait.
meals.dinner: Hyotei — one of Kyoto's most legendary and historic restaurants, holding three Michelin stars, serving refined kaiseki with a focus on morning porridge tradition and seasonal ingredients.

day_by_day.notes: Kyoto Imperial Palace tours require advance online reservation through the Imperial Household Agency. Fushimi Inari is best visited at dusk or early morning to avoid crowds. Hyotei reservations should be made months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Hiroshima via Shinkansen (approximately 1.5 hours from Kyoto). Begin with a profoundly moving visit to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park and Museum. Walk past the iconic A-Bomb Dome, lay flowers at the Children's Peace Monument, and spend reflective time in the museum learning about the events of August 6, 1945 — an essential and deeply educational experience for all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry ride from Hiroshima to the sacred Miyajima Island (Itsukushima). Marvel at the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine — one of Japan's most photographed landmarks — which appears to float on the water at high tide. Explore the shrine complex, stroll through the charming island village, and sample local Hiroshima specialties including momiji manju (maple leaf cakes) and fresh oysters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by Shinkansen in the early evening. Enjoy a quieter evening at the ryokan with a private onsen session and a light seasonal dinner, allowing time to reflect on the day's profound experiences.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the ryokan before departure — miso soup, rice, grilled salmon, and pickled vegetables.
meals.lunch: Kakifuku — a renowned Miyajima restaurant specializing in Hiroshima's famous oysters, served grilled, fried, and raw with local sake.
meals.dinner: In-ryokan private dinner — a lighter kaiseki selection featuring seasonal Kyoto vegetables, soba noodles, and warming broth dishes.

day_by_day.notes: The Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum is suitable for older children but may be emotionally intense — preview content beforehand if traveling with young children. Check ferry schedules to Miyajima in advance. The floating torii gate is best viewed at high tide — check tide charts before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Kyoto to Hakone via a combination of Shinkansen and the scenic Romancecar train — a luxurious and picturesque journey through the Japanese countryside. Check in to a premier onsen ryokan in Hakone with private open-air baths and views of Mount Fuji (weather permitting). Begin the afternoon with a visit to the Hakone Open-Air Museum, a remarkable outdoor sculpture park blending art with stunning mountain scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a scenic Hakone round course: ride the Hakone Ropeway over volcanic Owakudani Valley with views of steaming sulfur vents and (on clear days) Mount Fuji. Cruise across the serene Lake Ashi on a traditional pirate ship, with the iconic torii gate of Hakone Shrine rising from the water's edge. Visit the lakeside Hakone Shrine surrounded by ancient cedar trees.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the ryokan for a deeply restorative private rotenburo (outdoor hot spring bath) experience as the sun sets over the mountains. Indulge in a lavish multi-course kaiseki dinner at the ryokan, featuring locally sourced ingredients, Hakone spring water tofu, and seasonal mountain vegetables.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the Kyoto ryokan — full traditional Japanese spread.
meals.lunch: Fujiya Hotel Restaurant in Hakone — a historic and elegant dining institution serving French-Japanese fusion cuisine since 1878.
meals.dinner: In-ryokan kaiseki dinner — a 10-course seasonal menu featuring Hakone mountain vegetables, premium sashimi, wagyu beef, and local sake.

day_by_day.notes: Mount Fuji visibility is weather-dependent — April can be variable. Book the Hakone ryokan with private open-air baths (kashikiri onsen) for a fully exclusive experience. The Romancecar train from Shinjuku should be reserved in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for a private guided hike to a scenic Fuji viewpoint near Lake Kawaguchiko (approximately 30 minutes from Hakone) for the best chance of seeing Mount Fuji at sunrise — a breathtaking and iconic Japanese experience. Return to the ryokan for a leisurely breakfast before checking out and transferring back toward Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon exploring the refined Yanaka and Ueno districts of Tokyo. Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno — Japan's oldest and largest museum, housing an extraordinary collection of samurai armor, ancient pottery, Buddhist sculptures, and imperial artifacts. Stroll through Ueno Park, where late-blooming cherry trees may still offer a final glimpse of sakura season.
day_by_day.evening: Conclude your Tokyo experience with a farewell dinner at one of the city's most prestigious rooftop or view restaurants, offering panoramic night views of the Tokyo skyline. Afterward, take a private night tour of the illuminated Shibuya Crossing and Shinjuku entertainment district — a dazzling sensory finale to your Japan journey.

meals.breakfast: Full traditional Japanese breakfast at the Hakone ryokan — grilled fish, miso soup, rice, tamagoyaki, and seasonal pickles.
meals.lunch: Ueno Seiyoken — a historic French restaurant in Ueno Park that has been serving Tokyo's elite since 1876, offering refined Western cuisine in a classic setting.
meals.dinner: Kozue at Park Hyatt Tokyo (Shinjuku) — a Michelin-recognized Japanese restaurant on the 40th floor with sweeping city views and an exceptional seasonal menu.

day_by_day.notes: The pre-dawn Fuji hike requires a private guide and vehicle — arrange through the Hakone ryokan concierge. Weather permitting, sunrise views from Lake Kawaguchiko are among Japan's most iconic. Tokyo National Museum requires advance ticket booking during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final luxurious morning in Tokyo. Visit the Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning traditional Japanese garden nestled between modern skyscrapers, with a historic teahouse on a tidal pond. Participate in a private morning tea ceremony in the Nakajima no Ochaya teahouse, sipping matcha while gazing over the tranquil garden — a perfect, peaceful farewell to Japan.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your final afternoon in the upscale Omotesando and Aoyama districts for last-minute premium shopping — Japanese ceramics, lacquerware, high-end fashion, and artisan crafts. Visit Dover Street Market or the flagship stores of Japanese design brands like Issey Miyake and Comme des Garçons. Head to the hotel for final packing and checkout.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to the airport for your departure flight. Arrive with ample time to enjoy the premium lounges at Narita or Haneda Airport. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through Japan's most iconic landscapes, cultural treasures, and culinary wonders.

meals.breakfast: Premium hotel breakfast — a grand final spread featuring both Japanese and Western options, fresh-pressed juices, and artisan pastries.
meals.lunch: Florilège (Aoyama) — a Michelin two-star French-Japanese restaurant offering a refined lunch course that beautifully bridges Japanese ingredients with French technique.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or a farewell bento from Isetan's basement food hall (depachika) — curated premium Japanese delicacies including wagyu sushi, seasonal onigiri, and artisan sweets for the journey home.

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens teahouse matcha ceremony is a ticketed experience — book in advance. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport check-in and security. Consider purchasing premium Japanese gifts at the airport duty-free: whisky, wagashi, premium teas, and cosmetics.
